source_title: Ian McKellen pens moving tribute to Patrick Stewart
source_excerpt: Hollywood veteran Ian McKellen has paid an emotional tribute to his longtime friend and fellow actor Sir Patrick Stewart, remembering him as a proud Yorkshireman, an uncompromising truth-teller and one of the most respected actors of his generation.Stewart, who became a global icon as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in 'Star Trek' and Professor Charles Xavier in the 'X-Men' franchise, passed away on Wednesday, at the age of 86. In a statement issued by his family, he passed away in his home in Los Angeles, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia.Sharing a photograph of Stewart from the University of Huddersfield, McKellen penned a heartfelt note celebrating his friend's roots, illustrious career and enduring legacy. The tribute, dated October 29, also looked back at their first meeting as young actors with the Royal Shakespeare Company around five decades ago and the moment Stewart faced a career-defining decision that would eventually make him an international star.âSIR PATRICK STEWART (1940-2026),â McKellen began, âBefore everything else, Patrick was defined by being born and bred in Yorkshire, the proud county in the north of England which he loved to the end. You could hear it in his accented voice and in the stern honesty with which he told you what he thought and felt. Yorkshiremen have no truck with half-truths or avoidance of big issues. He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and in my case, love,â he wrote.Recalling their first meeting, McKellen wrote, âMy first strong memory was a few years later, meeting him in the street in central London when he told me about an offer to take over a leading part in 'Star Trek'. âBut Patrick think of your stage career in the UK. Do you really want to riskâgetting lost in Hollywood for years and years?ââ he recalled.Stewart ultimately took the leap, a decision McKellen believes audiences across the world were fortunate to witness. âAnd thank goodness for us all that he did for not just his devoted Trekkies but film and theatre audiences, who marvelled at his using international celebrity to star in a string of cinema successes ('X-Men' of course) and in great classical plays by Shakespeare, Ibsen, Arthur Miller, Peter Shaffer, Pinter and Beckett at Stratford-upon-Avon, in Londonâs West End and on Broadway,â McKellen wrote.The actor also reflected on Stewart's life in the United States, he said, âAmerica was his adopted home, where he met his adored Sunny who has cared for him through sickness and health, through thick and thin. But he never forsook his origins: and the proudest achievement of the most respected and beloved actor of his generation on either side of the Atlantic, was his appointment as Chancellor of Huddersfield University in Yorkshire.âMcKellen and Stewart are set to feature on screen in the upcoming Marvel film, 'Avengers: Doomsday'. The two actors famously played longtime friends turned adversaries Magneto and Professor X in the 'X-Men' franchise. A trailer for 'Avengers: Doomsday' has already offered fans a glimpse of the characters together, showing them sharing what appears to be one final game of chess against the backdrop of an impending catastrophe, brought on by Robert Downey Jr's Doctor Doom.McKellen ended his tribute by looking ahead to Stewart's final screen appearance, which is expected to bring his journey as Professor Charles Xavier to a close. âHis farewell performance in 'Avengers: Doomsday' is yet to be seen,â he concluded.'Avengers: Doomsday' will be released on December 18.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
